articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'The UK Direct Broadcast Satellite' (Digest No.10)

articleTitle: DMA 2280 and DMA 2285: processing of D2, D, C-MAC signals and descrambling
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on UK Direct Broadcast Satellite
abstract: The DMA 2285 is a digital real-time descrambling processor for both the D2-MAC and the D-MAC/packet system. Together with the appropriate D2- or D-MAC/Packet decoder chip 2280, it can be used to build up a D2- or D-MAC/Packet conditional access receiver. The programmable VLSI circuits in CMOS technology are housed in 68-pin PLCC packages and contain on a single silicon chip extensive functions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on UK Direct Broadcast Satellite
abstract: In July 1987, British Satellite Broadcasting (BSB) signed a 15 year contract with the IBA for the provision of three of the five DBS channels allocated to the United Kingdom under the World Administrative Radio Conference (WARC) agreement and plans. As the broadcasting agency for independent television, the IBA was tasked with the design, construction and operation of the broadcast uplink earth station.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The DMAC packet transmission system for UK DBS
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on UK Direct Broadcast Satellite
abstract: The forthcoming UK DBS service will use the DMAC/packet system, thus providing an evolutionary path for the addition of new services, starting from improved pictures and digital audio, and continuing right through to HDTV and multiple data services. The advantages offered by the system are described, together with the practical transmission system concepts and implementation. The anticipated four phases for developments both in transmissions and receiver technology are described, emphasizing the importance of the first phase of the set-top convertor in establishing a visible commercial service.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on UK Direct Broadcast Satellite
abstract: An important and novel aspect of the BSB transmissions is the inclusion of a conditional access (CA) system. This type of operation is new to UK broadcasting. It is used in the United States, but for much smaller operations than that of BSB. In addition the level of sophistication of BSB's CA system will be considerably higher than those used within the USA.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on UK Direct Broadcast Satellite
abstract: An overview of the planning and implementation of the BSB satellite control system. A brief summary of the operating characteristics of the satellite is provided and the methodology to deliver the satellite to its orbital location and operate it over its life is discussed. The primary ground control system and its emergency backup are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on UK Direct Broadcast Satellite
abstract: The IBA is to establish a satellite antenna footprint monitoring system to enable it to determine whether the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) specified in the BSB contract is maintained for each channel. This will be achieved by locating power flux density measuring equipment at five unmanned sites in the UK each being accessed from a master site. There will also be a sixth equipment available as a spare or transportable equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
